title: POC go/no-go criteria & benchmark plan - Veridian Health
next_steps: Redwood to share draft acceptance test spreadsheet by 2025-04-23
Customer to provide representative prompt set (<=200 samples) by 2025-04-21
Schedule on-prem smoke test window week of 2025-04-28
Agree final go/no-go thresholds in writing before test run (due 2025-04-25)
Redwood SE to provision dedicated trial capacity and provide connection details
action_items: Priya Nair: send draft SOW + acceptance spreadsheet by 2025-04-23
Carlos Mendes: prepare baseline benchmark runbook (QPS, seq len buckets) by 2025-04-22
Dr. Aaron Blake: deliver 150 representative prompts and golden outputs by 2025-04-21
Liam O'Connor: share data residency and KMS requirements (short doc) by 2025-04-22

summary: Alignment on POC acceptance tests: three-phase run (baseline, optimization, acceptance), explicit go/no-go thresholds for latency P95, token-cost target, and task-level quality (F1/accuracy). Reporting will be a CSV of raw runs plus a summary dashboard; single day acceptance run with pass criteria per metric. Timeline target is 2 weeks baseline/opt, 1-day acceptance test week of 2025-04-28.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-18 | 15:00 UTC | Duration ~46m
Attendees: Priya Nair, Carlos Mendes, Jordan Lee (Redwood); Dr. Aaron Blake, Meera Shah, Liam O'Connor, Ravi Patel, Ellie Tran (Veridian)
[00:00] Priya: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for carving out time. quick goal for today is to lock the success criteria for the POC and the acceptance test format so both sides can sign off.
[00:30] Dr. Aaron: thanks Priya, yeah we want to avoid vague outcomes — need clear go/no-go thresholds because this will drive procurement.
[01:10] Priya: totally. Carlos and I sketched a three-stage plan: baseline profiling, optimization & tuning, then a single acceptance window. baseline is two business weeks, optimization one to two weeks, acceptance test day is a single day run where we evaluate against thresholds.
[01:40] Carlos: (SE) and technically we'll provision a dedicated trial pool with pinned model versions. baseline will use default quantization; optimization stage we'll try 4-bit/8-bit and caching.
[02:05] Meera: quick question — what does the acceptance report look like? do we get raw logs or a dashboard?
[02:20] Jordan: both. our deliverable is a per-run CSV with tokens, latency per request, status codes, and a summary PDF + a live dashboard link for the acceptance day. the CSV is the canonical artifact for procurement.
[03:00] Priya: big-picture success metrics proposed: latency P95 <= 250ms for 512-token prompts at target concurrency; 99.9% availability during the run; model-level quality: task F1 >= 0.92 (or classification accuracy >= 92%) on your golden set; cost per 1k tokens <= $2.50 (trial adjusted).
[03:40] Liam: the cost number is less important for go/no-go than security. we need full KMS integration and audit logs retained for 90 days.
[03:55] Priya: understood — KMS + audit logs included in dedicated trial. we'll capture that in the SOW.
[04:30] Dr. Aaron: on the accuracy metric, we need to define how we compute F1 across multi-label clinical entity extraction — is Greenwood counting partial matches? (sic)
[04:45] Carlos: good point, we'll use strict token-span matching; for borderline cases include an error bucket. we'll put exact scoring code in the spreadsheet.
[05:20] Meera: also need edge-case tests for long context (2,048+ tokens) and short prompts — they behave differently.
[05:40] Carlos: yes we will bucket sequence lengths: 0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, 1025-2048+ and report per-bucket P95 and mean cost.
[06:15] Priya: workload sizing — please confirm expected concurrent QPS for acceptance run.
[06:30] Ravi: our target for production is ~120 concurrent requests sustained with bursts to 250 qps for 30s. for the POC acceptance we can run at 50% — so plan for 60 sustained, peak 125 for the run.
[06:55] Carlos: will run baseline at 60 concurrency, spike tests to 125 for 2x 30s windows. we'll also measure cold start under a 15-minute idle.
[07:25] Ellie: is caching allowed for acceptance? the product uses prefix caching heavily.
[07:35] Priya: caching is allowed but must be declared. acceptance will include a cold-start bucket (no cache) and warmed cache bucket; thresholds must be met in both or we agree weighted scoring.
[08:15] Dr. Aaron: can Redwood provide an objective failure mode report? e.g., skew between model variants, token truncation issues.
[08:40] Carlos: yes, we'll include a regression checklist: truncation, hallucination rate (we'll measure hallucination with a 50-case probe set), tokenization mismatches, and end-to-end latency per component.
[09:10] Meera: what about reporting format — column layout for CSV?
[09:25] Jordan: the CSV will include: run_id, timestamp_iso, prompt_id, seq_len_input, seq_len_output, tokens_in, tokens_out, total_tokens, latency_ms, p95_latency_bucket, status, model_revision, cache_hit_truefalse, cost_usd, accuracy_metric_value. plus a summary sheet with per-bucket aggregates.
[10:00] Liam: security checklist — SAML SSO for console access, RBAC for logs, KMS with customer-managed keys, encryption at rest and transit. can we get SOC 2 artifact?
[10:25] Priya: yes we will send SOC 2 report and our SOC auditor contact. SAML and CMK supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted trial we can enable KMS integration with an approved flow.
[11:00] Ravi: connectivity — we're likely to do the acceptance run from our staging VPC via a temporary VPN. we need IP allowlist details.
[11:20] Carlos: we'll provide egress IP ranges and transient keys for the test.
[12:00] (brief crosstalk)
[15:20] Priya: back to thresholds — let's walk through go/no-go logic. proposal: run-level pass requires meeting all three primary metrics: (1) latency P95 threshold <= 250ms for high-priority bucket, (2) task-level quality >= 0.92 F1, (3) no critical security failures (KMS/audit missing, data exfil events). if any are failed, we go to remediation loop and can re-run once within the trial window.
[16:05] Dr. Aaron: what's acceptable for marginal failures? e.g., F1 of 0.915 — do we fail immediately?
[16:20] Priya: propose a soft-fail margin: +/- 1% for quality metrics triggers a warning and root-cause review but still counts as a conditional pass pending tuning. we should capture this in the acceptance spreadsheet and in procurement language.
[17:00] Meera: also need to define sample size for the golden set. we propose minimum 100 labeled cases for primary metrics and additional 50 for hallucination probes.
[17:25] Carlos: yes we'll require at least 100 primary and 50 probe items; we recommend 200 to reduce variance.
[18:10] Priya: timeline recap: customer supplies prompts + golden outputs by 2025-04-21; baseline run week of 2025-04-22 (2 business days of profiling), optimization week 2025-04-28, acceptance day target 2025-05-02 (flexible).
[18:45] Dr. Aaron: procurement will want the exact acceptance matrix, we need that in the SOW.
[19:05] Priya: we'll embed the acceptance matrix in the SOW and the spreadsheet.
[20:15] (small tangential discussion about cost modeling)
[25:00] Carlos: technical note on metrics collection: our agent will emit structured logs to S3 with gzipped CSVs and a pre-built analysis notebook will compute pxx, cost, and quality. we'll share the notebook so you can re-run offline.
[25:40] Ravi: any special firewall requirements for S3 egress? we need presigned URLs only.
[26:00] Jordan: we'll support presigned uploads and a direct SFTP if you prefer.
[30:10] Meera: who owns final sign-off?
[30:25] Dr. Aaron: I'll own the technical sign-off, procurement will own commercial sign-off (Meera will coordinate), and Liam will confirm security sign-off.
[31:00] Priya: good — acceptance pack will be delivered to those three reps.
[35:30] (brief silence, leader confirms dates)
[36:10] Carlos: one more thing — for the optimization stage we'll test quantization variants (int8, int4 when available), batching heuristics, and cache policies. we'll include deterministic seeds for reproducibility.
[37:00] Ellie: do we need model eval harness in our environment or can we rely on Redwood's harness?
[37:20] Carlos: we'll give you the harness as a container you can run in staging; results must match Redwood's run for acceptance.
[38:10] Meera: any red flags we should know?
[38:25] Priya: nothing unusual — main risks are data transfer windows and prompt representativeness. if your prompt set is biased to short contexts we may overfit.
[39:05] Dr. Aaron: agreed. we'll try to include long and short samples.
[40:20] Priya: recap of deliverables from Redwood: acceptance spreadsheet + scoring code, baseline run CSVs, summary PDF, access to dashboard, SOC 2 and security artifacts, SOW draft. from Veridian: prompt set and golden outputs, IP allowlist, KMS requirements doc, procurement temps.
[41:05] Meera: timeline check again — we'll aim to have prompts to you by 4/21. purchasing team will give initial feedback 4/25.
[42:00] Priya: ok we'll aim to run baseline 4/22-4/23, optimization 4/28-5/01, acceptance 5/02. all tentative pending prompt delivery.
[42:45] (short housekeeping)
[45:00] Priya: final quick readback — acceptance criteria: P95 <=250ms, F1>=0.92 (with 1% soft margin), cost target <= $2.50/1k tokens, KMS/audit enabled. reporting: canonical CSV + dashboard + notebook. next actions: we will circulate the acceptance spreadsheet and SOW by 4/23. any objections?
[45:30] Dr. Aaron: none from us — looks good.
[45:45] Liam: sounds good from security too.
[46:00] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for run windows and the doc links. bye.
